content: 1. There is no FDA guidance regarding the use of the HPV vaccine in specific racial populations. 2. There is no FDA guidance on the use of the HPV vaccine in patients with renal impairment. 3. There is no FDA guidance on the use of the HPV vaccine in patients with hepatic impairment. 4. There is no FDA guidance on the use of the HPV vaccine in women of reproductive potential or in males. 5. The immunologic response to the quadrivalent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine may be diminished in immunocompromised individuals. 6. The HPV vaccine is administered via intramuscular injection. 7. There is limited information available regarding the monitoring of the HPV vaccine in the drug label. 8. There is limited information available regarding the compatibility of the HPV vaccine with intravenous (IV) administrations. 9. There have been reports of administration of higher-than-recommended doses of the quadrivalent HPV vaccine. 10. In general, the adverse event profile reported with overdose was comparable to that observed with the recommended single doses of the quadrivalent HPV vaccine. 11. HPV infects only human beings. 12. Animal studies with analogous animal papillomaviruses suggest that the efficacy of L1 virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines may involve the development of humoral immune responses. 13. Human beings develop a humoral immune response to the vaccine, although the exact mechanism of protection remains unknown. 14. GARDASIL, the quadrivalent HPV vaccine (types 6, 11, 16, and 18), is a non-infectious recombinant vaccine prepared from purified virus-like particles (VLPs) of the major capsid (L1) protein of HPV types 6, 11, 16, and 18. 15. The L1 proteins are produced by separate fermentations in recombinant Saccharomyces cerevisiae and self-assembled into VLPs. 16. The fermentation process involves the growth of Saccharomyces cerevisiae on chemically defined fermentation media, which include vitamins, amino acids, mineral salts, and carbohydrates. 17. The VLPs are released from the yeast cells by cell disruption and purified using a series of chemical and physical methods. 18. The purified VLPs are adsorbed onto a preformed aluminum-containing adjuvant (amorphous aluminum hydroxyphosphate sulfate). 19. The quadrivalent HPV VLP vaccine is a sterile liquid suspension prepared by combining the adsorbed VLPs of each HPV type with additional amounts of the aluminum-containing adjuvant and the final purification buffer. 20. The quadrivalent HPV vaccine is a sterile suspension intended for intramuscular administration. 21. Each 0.5-mL dose contains approximately 20 mcg of HPV 6 L1 protein, 40 mcg of HPV 11 L1 protein, 40 mcg of HPV 16 L1 protein, and 20 mcg of HPV 18 L1 protein. 22.
